# Complex power series

Geometric and exponential series give power-series representations of elementary complex functions.

## Exercises

:::{#exr-complex-power-series-consider-taylor-series-th-partial-sum}

Consider the geometric series $$\sum_{n=0}^\infty z^n  = 1 + z + z^2 + \ldots \longrightarrow \frac{1}{1-z}.$$ Show that the $N$th partial sum is

$$
\sum_{n=0}^{N}z^n=\frac{1-z^{N+1}}{1-z}.
$$

Polynomial long division may be useful.

:::

:::{#exr-complex-power-series-find-upper-bound-such-partial-sum}

Find an upper bound for $|z|$ such that the partial sum converges to $1/(1-z)$.

:::

:::{#exr-complex-power-series-taylor-series-exponential-function-definition-complex}

The Taylor series for the exponential function is $$\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{1}{n!} z^n.$$ Using the definition of the complex exponential, find the Taylor series for $\cos(x)$ and $\sin(x)$, for $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

:::

:::{#exr-complex-power-series-make-plots-partial-sums-sine-cosine}

Make plots of the partial sums of the sine and cosine Taylor series to verify your result.

:::

:::{#exr-complex-power-series-find-taylor-series-function}

Find the Taylor series for the function $f(z) = (e^z - 1)/z$

:::

:::{#exr-complex-power-series-find-taylor-series-function-2}

Find the Taylor series for the function $f(z) = \sin(z)/z$ for $z\neq 0$ and $f(0) = 1$.

:::
